impl.summary:
I finished the C-helper and capture-framework part (A1-A3, B1-B8, C, D). The C tests and kismet_e2e.sh all pass. I proved each item in WSL with fake boards on ptys, a before/after build and Kismets on 2601/3601; logs are in the evidence folder. Nothing was committed. The tree at /root/src/kismet is patched, rebuilt incrementally and installed (capture_framework.c.o rebuilt, all 18 compiled kismet_cap_* relinked). Note: another process is currently running remote_e2e.sh against that install on 2731.

**Framework patches (add-to-kismet.sh).** Each is a python3 edit with exact anchors, idempotent, and skipped with a printed note if the code has changed. I checked them on a pristine cfe427074 copy (applied twice) and got a result identical to the built tree.
- **A1:** the two send paths now call lws_cancel_service() instead of lws_callback_on_writable(), and a new LWS_CALLBACK_EVENT_WAIT_CANCELLED case asks for the write on the service thread (under handler_lock, using caph->lwsclientwsi because lws passes a stand-in wsi there). No other lws_callback_on_writable call runs off the service thread.
  - I added one thing you didn't ask for: cf_handler_spindown now wakes the websocket loop, and a WRITEABLE callback with nothing queued and spindown set ends the connection. Without it, a capture that ends after its last frame leaves the helper connected forever; before A1 the 5 s delay hid this.
  - A1 goes in whole or not at all, because the wake-ups alone would never write anything.
- **A2:** LWS_CALLBACK_CLIENT_CLOSED also calls lws_cancel_service().
- **A3:** user, password and API key are percent-encoded, keeping only RFC 3986 unreserved characters.
- The header now lists all four upstream fixes and says the script needs python3.

**Helper changes (capture_esp32c5.c):**
- **B1:** the 15 s give-up text and the send-failure text go to Kismet as a MSGFLAG_ERROR message first, then as the ERROR frame. Both are queued before spindown, and the framework flushes them before exiting.
- **B2:** "capturing" is only said once the PCAP header has the right link type. The 15 s clock and the handshake now use "capturing", not just "synced". The parser rule is unchanged.
- **B3:** the remote capture child (retry on, `monitor_pid==0`) gets PR_SET_PDEATHSIG. A pthread_atfork hook records the parent pid for the race check. Remote processes also clear the port's exclusive mode (TIOCNXCL) on SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP, then die by the signal.
- **B4:** the remote probe refuses a port another process has flock'd. The /proc/locks lookup now ignores the helper's own pid. The framework probes before every TCP and websocket connection, so the check runs on each retry.
- **B5:** in BTLE mode, channels 38 and 39 are rewritten to "37" in the framework's own writable string (that string is what the framework reports back), and other channels are refused.
- **B6:** lws_set_log_level(LLL_ERR|LLL_WARN) is set before the lws context is created.
- **B7:** every packet carries a signal block with the frequency:
  - **Wi-Fi:** only freq_khz, taken from the radiotap Channel field; no block if there is no Channel field.
  - **802.15.4:** channel string, signal_dbm (RSS rounded half away from zero, left out when absent or 0) and freq_khz = (2405+5*(ch-11))*1000.
  - **BTLE:** only freq_khz = 2402000.
  - This matches what the Python helper already sends.
- **B8:** the chancontrol comment and the header docs describe all of the above.

**Another addition you didn't ask for: a websocket PING watchdog.** In WSL, the evicted-helper problem (n5b) turned out not to involve CLIENT_CLOSED at all. When a second connection takes a running source's uuid, Kismet closes the source but leaves its websocket open, and simply stops sending PINGs. The framework's websocket loop, unlike its TCP loop, never checks for missing PINGs. So the capture thread now closes the connection after 15 s without a PING, and the framework reconnects. Kismet's close doesn't wait for the old connection to close before the new one replaces it, which is why the old websocket is left open.

**Proofs (before → after):**
- **A1:** first packet at 5.20 s → 1.00 s. Before, sendto calls came in bursts at :20.9, :26.0 and :31.0; after, about 98 sendto calls every second. Before, 17 of 100 polls showed new packets; after, 95 of 100, with no flat stretch.
- **A2, close_source.cmd:** the child exits in 0.26 s both before and after, releases the flock, and reconnects 5.3 s later.
- **A2, same-uuid eviction:** before, the child held the flock for 40 s+ on a silent, still-open websocket. After, "ERROR: c6-a2: no PING from Kismet for 15 seconds; closing the connection" at t=15 s, the flock is released, and it reconnects at t=20 s.
  - A variant build without the spindown wake closed the port at 15 s but stayed connected and never reconnected, which shows that part is needed.
- **A3:** with password `pa ss%41x`, the new helper logs in (source running, 701 packets); the old one repeats "FATAL: Datasource could not connect websocket client". With `a&b`, the helper prints the warning and gets 401. The warning also fires when the password comes from KISMET_CAP_PASSWORD.
- **B1:**
  - **Websocket, silent board:** after the fix, Kismet logs "ERROR: c6-b1 - c6-b1: no capture from the board on /dev/pts/3 for 15 seconds; ...". Before, this line never appeared.
  - **Local source:** kismet_e2e.sh checks the same thing and passes.
- **B3:** after kill -TERM of the parent, the child and its flock are gone within 0.1 s. Before, the child was re-parented and kept the flock.
- **B4:**
  - **Before:** the remote helper evicted the local source ("matches existing source 'c6-local' ... will be closed").
  - **After:** it was refused three times while the local source kept capturing (18 → 1250 packets), and took over 2.5 s after close_source.cmd.
  - **Legacy TCP and no retry:** TCP behaves the same. With --disable-retry the exit status is 0 over websocket and 4 over TCP; these are the framework's own codes, the same as for a missing board.
- **B5:** before, set_channel 38/39/40 showed 38/39/40; after, 38 and 39 show 37 and 40 is refused.
- **B6:** the "N:" lines are gone, including "getsockopt fd N says e 111" (a NOTICE in lws 4.3.3 and 4.3.5). The two "W: _lws_smd_msg_send: rejecting message on queue depth 40" lines remain. They come from lws's netlink route and address dump at context creation, which overflows its default queue of 40 messages. They are harmless and unrelated to A1 (same count before and after). The only real fix is for the framework to set lwsinfo.smd_queue_depth; I left them visible rather than hide them.
- **B7:** in kismetdb, `packets.frequency` is 2437000 for Wi-Fi but 0 for 802.15.4 and BTLE whatever any helper sends. Kismet's 802.15.4 and BTLE phy handlers never fill the field that column reads. The device records are right: 802.15.4 2425000/2475000, BTLE 2402000, Wi-Fi 2437000/5180000/5745000.

**Tests added:** test_parser.c checks the "capturing" rules at every chunk size, all three signal blocks and the radiotap parser, the remote busy refusal, BTLE channel sets, the send-failure message, the watchdog, TIOCNXCL on SIGTERM (with a control), PDEATHSIG including the race and a control, URI encoding through the patched framework, and the '&' warning. kismet_e2e.sh adds device-frequency checks, BTLE set_channel 38 reported as 37, and a firmware-without-radio case (lost sync said once, no "capturing", the 15 s reason in Kismet's log). fake_board.py gains --lacks RADIO and --silent.

impl.tests:
Everything ran in WSL (Ubuntu, lws 4.3.3) against /root/src/kismet (cfe427074 patched by this add-to-kismet.sh) and /root/kismet-install.
- tests/c/run.sh as root: 297 PASS, ALL OK (was 259 before; the two old port-lock checks that failed against the changed helper were rewritten to hold the lock from another process).
- The same test binary as nobody (setpriv): 275 PASS, 2 SKIP (root-only), ALL OK.
- tests/kismet_e2e.sh with KISMET=/root/kismet-install/bin/kismet: 55 PASS, ALL OK. It ran once before and once after the frequency assertions were added.
- Manual before/after proofs on Kismets at 2601/3601 (plus a fake websocket server on 2602), summarised in <case>.summary.txt with full logs in <case>/:
  - A1: a1-before, a1-after
  - A2: a2-before, a2-before-strace, a2c-before, a2c-after, a2-evict-after, a2-evict-variant-no-spindown-wake, a2t-before
  - A3: a3-space-before, a3-space-after, a3-amp-after, a3-amp-env
  - B1: b1-before, b1-after, b1-variant-no-spindown-wake
  - B3: b3-before, b3-after
  - B4: b4-before, b4-after, b4b-after
  - B5: b5-before, b5-after
  - B6: b6
  - B7: b7 (kismetdb queries and the .kismet file)
- Build logs, per-file diffs, the patched capture_framework.c and its diff against upstream are in tests/; the proof scripts are in scripts/.
- I did not run the Python unit tests: they belong to the other agent and import none of my files.
- I installed strace, sqlite3 and bc with apt in WSL for these runs. My WSL working folder /root/c-agent-fix6 (before binaries, variant build, scripts) is left in place; no test processes or /tmp dirs of mine remain.
open_issues: A2's own mechanism (CLIENT_CLOSED firing from lws's timers, after which lws_service goes back to sleep) did not reproduce in WSL. Every close I produced came through socket servicing and ended the loop at once, before and after the patch: Kismet exiting, close_source.cmd, a server CLOSE frame (fake server) and the helper's own close. The patch is in place and harmless. The Pi's n5b symptom showed up here as a different problem: Kismet never closes the evicted websocket. The PING watchdog plus A1's spindown wake fix that. The exact Pi sequence ('FATAL: Datasource websocket closed' with no 'capture process exited') was not reproduced.

Kismet server bug, not patched: when a connection arrives with a running source's uuid, Kismet closes the source without waiting (kis_datasource::close_external has ft.wait() commented out), then swaps io_ to the new connection. The posted close then hits the new connection ('Error reconnecting remote source ... - source closed / failed to send v3 OPENREQ'), and the old websocket stays open and silent forever. Consequence: two remote helpers with the same uuid on different boards (a misconfiguration) now take turns every ~20 s. Before, one of them hung silently holding its board. B4 prevents the realistic cases (same board, or a local source on the same machine).

The 'W: _lws_smd_msg_send: rejecting message on queue depth 40' warnings remain. Cause: lws's netlink role reports about one SMD message per kernel route and interface address at context creation, and the default queue holds 40. They are harmless: only lws's own captive-portal trigger listens, and the framework doesn't use it. A proper fix would be an upstream framework change setting lwsinfo.smd_queue_depth; I did not do it.

Local sources: Kismet now logs the helper's 15 s reason, but the source's error_reason is still 'IPC connection closed', because Kismet ignores the ERROR frame (e2e noradio: error='IPC connection closed').

The framework reports a channel the helper refuses (chancontrol returning 0) as success with the old channel, so Kismet returns HTTP 200 and the channel is unchanged. The refusal text only reaches the helper's stderr (e.g. 'INFO: c6-b5 cannot tune to channel 40 in btle mode'). This is pre-existing framework behaviour, the same as for Wi-Fi refusals.

With --disable-retry, a refused busy port exits with status 0 over the websocket and 4 over --tcp (the framework's own codes, same as a missing board). Neither is documented as a distinct status; I did not add one.

kismetdb: packets.frequency is 0 for 802.15.4 and BTLE from any helper, and most BTLE packets are logged with phyname 'Unknown' (1864 vs 2 in b7). Both are Kismet behaviour, not the helpers'. Device records carry the right frequency.

Unverified idea, no change made: if the framework cancels the capture thread (pthread_cancel at loop exit) while it holds local->lock inside write_all during a handshake, a hopping hop thread could block and cf_handler_shutdown would deadlock on handler_lock. I did not observe this and don't think it explains n5b.

The wiki (docs/wiki, not my files) needs updates:
- Command-Line-Reference: the note on space/%XX logins is now fixed ('&' is still impossible); add the new warning, busy-port, PING-watchdog and PDEATHSIG texts.
- Troubleshooting and Bluetooth-LE-Capture: the reason now reaches Kismet's log; BTLE set_channel 38/39 shows 37, other channels are refused.
- Channel-Control: kismet.datasource.channel stays at the start channel while hopping.
- Development-and-Testing: new fake_board options, new e2e cases, run.sh coverage.
The Pi hardware stage was not part of my work, so these changes have not run on the Pi or on real boards.

review.summary:
I reviewed the C helper and capture-framework part: kismet/add-to-kismet.sh, capture_esp32c5.c, Makefile.in, tests/c, kismet_e2e.sh and fake_board.py, against the originals in c-agent/orig, upstream cfe427074 and the Python helper. I found six problems (two medium, four low), all demonstrated below.

**What held up in my own runs:**
- **C tests:** tests/c/run.sh passes (297 PASS, ALL OK). tests/kismet_e2e.sh passes (55 PASS, ALL OK).
- **Idempotence:** I applied add-to-kismet.sh to a fresh `git archive cfe427074` twice. The second run changed nothing, and the resulting capture_framework.c is byte-identical to /root/src/kismet's. Applying it over a tree already patched by the old script adds exactly the three new edits, with the same result.
- **lws threading:** The framework patch looks right. The only remaining lws_callback_on_writable calls run on the service thread (the WRITEABLE callback and EVENT_WAIT_CANCELLED). lws_cancel_service is the only lws call made from other threads, and the lws context is never destroyed, so there is no use-after-free.
- **PING watchdog:** It works. During an eviction Kismet keeps draining the evicted websocket (Recv-Q 0 on both sides the whole time), so the helper cannot block on a full ring before the watchdog fires; the child ended about 15 s after the last PING.
- **Signal blocks:** The C and Python helpers send the same blocks.
- **Makefile.in header:** Accurate.

**Suspected but not demonstrated (not in the findings):**
- **Shutdown race:** The framework cancels the capture thread asynchronously (PTHREAD_CANCEL_ASYNCHRONOUS). The spindown wake now ends the websocket loop right after the capture thread's first cf_handler_spindown, and cf_int_capture_thread then calls cf_handler_spindown a second time. A cancel that lands while that second call holds handler_lock would hang cf_handler_shutdown. The window is microseconds; TCP and local sources already have the same pattern upstream.
- **Wall-clock watchdog:** It uses time(), as the framework's TCP check does. A Pi's NTP jump at boot can force one spurious reconnect.
- **Long logins:** After 3x percent-encoding, the 1024-byte URI buffer can silently truncate a very long login.
- **Spurious warning:** The '&' warning also fires for `--apikey K --user 'a&b'` with no password, although the framework then logs in with the API key.
- **Busy-port message:** On a busy port, the C helper's framework prints the FATAL "already in use" line on every 5 s retry; the Python helper says it once.
- **BTLE hop list:** A BTLE hop list is reported back as 37,37,37 (the Python helper does the same).

I made no repo edits. Scripts and outputs are in C:\Users\oshria\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\c--Users-oshria-OneDrive-Documents-GitHub-esp32c5-wireshark-sniffer\75fe8a4e-1aa2-48f3-9e8d-8f12a0275438\scratchpad\fix6\c-review (scripts\, outputs\, and one folder per case). My WSL temp dir /tmp/crev (Kismet copies, mutants, binaries) has been removed, and none of my processes are left running.

findings.title: catch_end_signals replaces an inherited SIG_IGN, so a remote helper started with nohup (or as a background job in a script) now dies on SIGHUP/SIGINT
findings.demonstration:
Setup: WSL, Kismet on 2621, fake board on a pty. Command: `nohup kismet_cap_esp32c5 --connect 127.0.0.1:2621 ... [--disable-retry] &`, wait 6 s, then `kill -HUP` its processes, as a closed terminal does (script: c-review\scripts\hup.sh).

New helper, --disable-retry (outputs\hup-new-noretry.txt):
  'helper 259781 (SigIgn 0000000000001004)' -> after SIGHUP: 'Hangup ... nohup $HELPER'; 'helper alive=no ... packets 503 running=0' for the next 8 s.

Original helper, same run (outputs\hup-orig-noretry.txt):
  'SigIgn 0000000000001007'; 'helper alive=yes ... packets 602 ... 1323 running=1'.

New helper with retry (outputs\hup-new-retry.txt):
  parent 'SigIgn 0000000000000007' (HUP, INT and QUIT ignored), capture child 'SigIgn 0000000000001004' (the handler has replaced SIG_IGN for HUP and INT).
  After SIGHUP: 'INFO: capture process exited 0 signal 1'; running=0 and packets stuck at 507 for about 5 s, then a reconnect.

SA_RESETHAND then puts SIG_DFL back, not SIG_IGN, so the raise() kills the process.
findings.suggested_fix: In catch_end_signals, read each signal's current action first (`sigaction(sig, NULL, &old)`) and leave it alone when `old.sa_handler == SIG_IGN`. This is the usual rule for programs that install termination handlers: nohup, and shells without job control, ignore SIGHUP and SIGINT on purpose. Mention in the comment that an ignored signal stays ignored.

findings.title: No test exercises the C helper as a remote helper: main()'s new remote wiring can be broken with every test still passing
findings.demonstration:
Mutation script: c-review\scripts\mut.sh. It edits a copy of capture_esp32c5.c and runs tests/c/run.sh against /root/src/kismet.

Every one of these mutants passes run.sh with 297 PASS and ALL OK (outputs\mut-*.log):
- `pthread_atfork(note_fork, NULL, NULL);` removed
- `catch_end_signals(&local);` removed
- `end_with_parent();` removed
- `lws_set_log_level(...)` removed

kismet_e2e.sh cannot catch them: it has no remote case (`grep -c -- --connect tests/kismet_e2e.sh` prints 0). remote_e2e.sh's start_helper runs only `$PYTHON -m esp32c5_kismet.remote`.

The atfork mutant breaks remote capture completely. forked_from stays 0, so end_with_parent raises SIGTERM in every capture child. Built and run with retry against Kismet 2621 for 12 s (outputs\retry-noatfork.txt): 'running= packets=' and 'INFO: capture process exited 0 signal 15' / 'Sleeping 5 seconds ...' three times.

The framework's websocket patches (the A1 wake, the A2 wake on close, the spindown wake) likewise run in no automated test; they have only the manual proofs.

findings.title: PR_SET_PDEATHSIG is silently cleared when a setuid-root helper opens a port the user owns (setfsuid in open_port), so the capture child outlives its parent
findings.demonstration:
Script: c-review\scripts\suid.sh. Setup: the new helper installed setuid root (chmod 4755) and run by nobody through setpriv, with retry, on a fake board run by nobody (pty 'crw--w---- 1 nobody tty /dev/pts/3'). After the capture starts, `kill -TERM` the parent.

Result (outputs\suid-new.txt):
  'parent 261322 (uid/euid 65534 0), capture child 261324; running=1 packets=507; flock holders: 261324'
  then 'parent alive=no; child alive=yes (ppid 261178); flock holders: 261324 ; packets=714'.
  The orphan keeps capturing and holding the port.

Control: the same setuid helper run by nobody, but on a root-owned pty, so no EACCES and no setfsuid (outputs\suid-new-rootpty.txt): 'parent alive=no; child alive=no; flock holders: ; packets=508'.

Cause: open_callback runs on the main thread, the one that called prctl. Its open_port gets EACCES and calls setfsuid(getuid()); the kernel's commit_creds zeroes task->pdeath_signal on any fsuid change.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-arm the parent-death signal after the fsuid switch. For example, keep a static flag set by end_with_parent; in open_port, after `setfsuid((uid_t) was)`, call prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGTERM) again when the flag is set, then repeat the getppid() != forked_from check. Only the arming thread needs it, since the setting is per thread. Also note in end_with_parent's comment that a credential change clears the setting.

findings.title: BTLE channel set outside 37-39: the C helper reports success to Kismet while the Python helper reports failure and closes the source
findings.demonstration:
Script: c-review\scripts\btle40.sh. Setup: a remote BTLE source on a fake board, Kismet 2621; `set_channel.cmd {"channel": "40"}`.

C helper (outputs\btle40-c.txt):
  'set_channel 40: HTTP 200'; after: 'running=1 error=0 error_reason= channel=37'.
  Kismet's log has only 'setting channel 40'; the refusal appears only on the helper's stderr ('INFO: rv-b40 cannot tune to channel 40 in btle mode').

Python helper, same run (outputs\btle40-py.txt):
  'HTTP 500'; 'running=0 error=1 error_reason=40 is not a channel the board can tune to in btle mode'.
  Kismet logs 'failed to set channel 40'.

Python's own comment (remote.py:912: 'the C tool quits too') is wrong about C: chancontrol_callback returns 0, and the framework turns that into a successful CONFIGREPORT.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide on one behaviour for both helpers and document it on the wiki. If a refused channel should fail in Kismet, return -1 from chancontrol_callback for the BTLE (and Wi-Fi/802.15.4) refusals: the framework then sends a failed CONFIGREPORT with the message and ends the connection, as the Python helper does. Otherwise, change the Python helper and fix its comment. Either way, the channel-set text on the wiki must match both helpers.

findings.title: The '&' login warning misses getopt_long's abbreviated options (--pass, --passw, --use ...), which the framework accepts
findings.demonstration:
Script: c-review\scripts\pass.sh, against Kismet 2621 (outputs\pass.txt).
- `--pass rv-password`: 'running=1 packets=501', so getopt_long takes --pass as --password.
- `--pass 'a&b'`: no WARNING line; only 'W: ... got bad HTTP response '401'' and 'FATAL: Datasource could not connect websocket client'.
- `--password 'a&b'`: prints 'WARNING: the Kismet user name or password contains '&' ...'.

is_option() matches only the exact option names. login_from_env shares the gap: it does not see --pass as a password either.
findings.suggested_fix: In warn_login_ampersand (and login_from_env), recognise any unambiguous prefix of --user, --password and --apikey, as getopt_long does. Alternatively, run the check after cf_handler_parse_opts on the parsed login; for example, test caph->lwsuri's decoded user and password, or have the framework expose them.

findings.title: test_say_why claims to check that the MESSAGE goes before the ERROR, but passes with the order reversed
findings.demonstration:

fix.summary:
I reproduced all six of the reviewer's findings and fixed each one, with tests. I also closed three of the reviewer's suspected issues and made a flaky end-to-end check reliable. Nothing was committed.

**Fixes in `kismet/capture_esp32c5/capture_esp32c5.c`:**
- **Ignored signals stay ignored.** `catch_end_signals` now skips a signal the helper was started with ignored, so `nohup` keeps SIGHUP ignored and a background job keeps SIGINT ignored.
- **Parent-death signal is set again after `open_port`.** When the helper is installed setuid root and opens a port the user owns, it switches the file-system uid, which clears the signal. `open_port` now reads `PR_GET_PDEATHSIG` first and calls `end_with_parent` again afterwards, including its race check.
- **Refused channel sets reach Kismet's log.** A refused channel set still returns 0, the way Kismet's own helpers refuse one: the capture keeps running on its old channel. The refusal now also goes to Kismet as an error message. This happens for channel sets only, not hops.
- **The login is read the way the framework reads it.** A new `read_login_args` parses the command line with `getopt_long` and a copy of the framework's option table. So abbreviations like `--pass` and `--use` count, and a word that is another option's value does not. `login_from_env` and the '&' warning both use it. The warning now fires only when the framework will actually log in with a user and a password.

**Fixes from the reviewer's suspected list and the implementer's open issues:**
- **PING watchdog uses the monotonic clock.** A Raspberry Pi's clock jumping when it syncs over the network after boot no longer forces a reconnect.
- **Capture thread no longer spins down itself.** The framework already does it after the thread returns. Doing it twice left a window where the framework could cancel the thread while it held the handler lock, and the process would hang on exit. The send-failure path still spins down twice (see open issues).
- **The bare-esp32c5 end-to-end check is no longer flaky.** It samples the source's error every second instead of reading it once at the end. The flake is Kismet's: the pre-fix helper failed the old check 3 times in 8 runs, the new one once in 8.

**New tests:**
- **End-to-end remote case.** `tests/kismet_e2e.sh` has a remote websocket case with 10 checks. A mutant helper missing any one of the atfork call, the signal handlers, the parent-death signal or the log level fails it. So does the pre-fix helper, and the fixed helper built against the unpatched framework (first packet at 5440 ms).
- **BTLE channel 40.** The e2e now sets BTLE to channel 40 and checks that Kismet logs the refusal.

`add-to-kismet.sh`, `Makefile.in` and `fake_board.py` are unchanged from the implementer's version. Re-running `add-to-kismet.sh` made no framework edits. Only `kismet_cap_esp32c5` was rebuilt, and it was installed atomically.

I decided that both helpers should do what Kismet's own helpers do: capture_linux_wifi returns 0 when a channel set fails, and catsniffer and ti_cc_2531 return 1. On a failed report, Kismet would call trigger_error and close the source, which stops capture over a typo.

findings.why:
Reproduced with the pre-fix helper (outputs/pass-btle40.txt):

The warning fires only when the framework will log in with a user and a password, since it uses them whenever it has both.

After the fix, `--pass 'a&b'` prints the warning, and `--pass <password>` with KISMET_CAP_USER captures (running=1, 511 packets).

On the reviewer's other point: from the framework source, `--apikey K --user 'a&b'` with no password does not log in with the key. The framework stops with 'Must specify both username and password'. With this fix it no longer warns there.

open_issues: The Python helper needs to match the channel-refusal behaviour I chose for C. esp32c5_kismet/remote.py configure() answers a refused channel set with a failed CONFIGREPORT and closes the source (HTTP 500; Kismet puts the source in error). The C helper answers success with the unchanged channel, keeps capturing, and sends the refusal to Kismet as an error MESSAGE. The comment at remote.py:912 ('the C tool quits too') was never true: the C helper has always returned 0 there. I recommend the Python helper send configreport(seqno, True, ..., channel=self.channel) plus an error message, and not close. The wiki's channel-set text must describe the behaviour both helpers end up with.

A Kismet race that predates this work, not fixable in the helper: when a local source's open fails (bare esp32c5, no board), Kismet sometimes starts two re-opens at once. One of them ends with 'FATAL: Remote side closed read pipe', and 'IPC connection closed' replaces the helper's reason as the source's error until the next attempt. That happened in 3 of 8 runs with the pre-fix helper and 1 of 8 with the new one. The e2e check now samples every second.

The send-failure path (send_packet) still spins down twice, in the helper and then in the framework's cf_int_capture_thread. That leaves the asynchronous-cancel window on handler_lock open for that rare path; the normal ends (the 15 s give-up, the PING watchdog, a spindown by the framework) now spin down once. Closing it would take a flag so that consume() and the capture loop stop without cf_handler_spindown. I did not do it.

The 'W: _lws_smd_msg_send: rejecting message on queue depth 40' warnings remain. A possible fifth framework patch would set lwsinfo.smd_queue_depth, guarded by LWS_WITH_SYS_SMD, before lws_create_context. I did not do it.

- A2's own mechanism (a close from lws timers) was not reproduced.
- Kismet's server leaves an evicted websocket open (close_external does not wait).

impl.summary:
Python remote helper side of the Pi-retest fixes (P1-P7), matched to the C agent's current capture_esp32c5.c (re-read after it changed at 12:10).

P1 board.py: BoardLink gains a `capturing` flag. "<port> capturing" (Python wording kept) is only reported once the PCAP header after our marker has the mode's link type (framer.need_global_hdr cleared), not at the marker. A wrong-firmware board now gives exactly [('<port> opened','opened'), ('<port>: lost sync (the board sends link type 283, not 127)','lost')] however often it is re-asked (test). Connection._watchdog uses link.capturing, so a board answering in the wrong link type is given up after 15 s too.

P2 board.port_locked(device, platform=None, locks='/proc/locks'): Linux only; stats the node (follows links), matches FLOCK lines on '%02x:%02x:%d' dev:inode, ignores this pid (same test as the C helper's node_locked()). RemoteSource.available() runs after resolve() and before connect(): a held port is not offered; WARNING once (then DEBUG), retried every RECONNECT_BACKOFF_S (5 s) while other sources run; text aligned to the C probe's. --list leaves held boards out (all three names), prints a 'Left out' line, exit 1 when nothing is left. Windows: no check (a trial open would toggle DTR/RTS). E2E proof (scratchpad p2_proof.txt, p2/timeline.txt): 'pid 213377 holds the flock on /dev/pts/4', '/proc/locks: 22: FLOCK  ADVISORY  WRITE 213377 00:6b:7 0 EOF'; for 12 s Kismet shows only 'free-b running=1 packets=0..140' (no held-a); 't=12605 ms: the holder is gone'; 't=15444 ms: ... held-a running=1 packets=0', 't=17977 ms: ... held-a running=1 packets=8'; 'released -> held-a a source in Kismet: 2839 ms; with packets: 5374 ms'. (That run predates aligning the text to the C wording.) Final e2e run: 'holding /dev/pts/5; released: offered after 307 ms, capturing in Kismet after 3183 ms' and '12:33:00 WARNING: fake-held: /tmp/esp32c5-remote-e2e.YBi41e/port-held is already in use by another capture; not offering it to Kismet until it is free (looked at again every 5 seconds)'. The e2e lock case also shows a second copy of the very same source is not offered and Kismet's log has no 'The running instance will be closed' (FACTS 7).

P3: BTLE reports '37' at open (unchanged), in the CONFIGREPORT for a channel set of 37/38/39, and for each hop-list entry of 37-39 (the C framework reports its hop list the same way: its chantranslate rewrites 38/39 to 37 in place). Parity with the C's new chancontrol: any other BTLE channel is refused with the existing Python text '<n> is not a channel the board can tune to in btle mode' (connection ends and is re-offered, as for Wi-Fi/zigbee). E2E: set_channel 38 -> HTTP 200, REST channel '37', hopping 0.

P4: '1 ... every source ended by itself' was unreachable (RemoteSource.run catches everything; only stop ends a source), so the text was fixed. Final rule: 0 = stopped by Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Break (Windows) or SIGTERM, --help, or --list listed a board; 1 = --list listed no board (none plugged in, or on Linux every one in use by another capture), or an internal error (every source thread died -- now logged as such -- or a traceback); 2 = a mistake on the command line or in a definition, or websocket-client missing without --tcp.

P5: signal block now carries freq_khz for all three radios: Wi-Fi from the radiotap Channel field (remote.radiotap_freq_khz; presence bits, TSFT/Flags/Rate stepped over, extended presence words; no block without a Channel field), 802.15.4 2405+5*(ch-11) MHz (unchanged, with channel and dBm), BTLE 2402000 (freq only). Same algorithm/blocks as the C agent's new code. kismetdb check (freq_check*.txt, fake boards, Kismet 2711): Wi-Fi packets.frequency 2437000/5180000/5745000; 802.15.4 and BTLE packets.frequency 0.0 for BOTH the Python helper and the C helper (new build 12:20:38, which also sends freq for all three); devices show 802.15.4 2425000/2475000 and BTLE 2402000. review.summary:
I reviewed the Python remote-helper side of fix6 (esp32c5_kismet/board.py, esp32c5_kismet/remote.py, tests/test_board.py, tests/test_kismet_v3.py, tests/remote_e2e.sh). I compared it with the current capture_esp32c5.c and with Kismet cfe427074, and did all runs in scratch copies (WSL /tmp/rvpy, cleaned up afterwards). Evidence is in C:\Users\oshria\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\c--Users-oshria-OneDrive-Documents-GitHub-esp32c5-wireshark-sniffer\75fe8a4e-1aa2-48f3-9e8d-8f12a0275438\scratchpad\fix6\review-py (mut.py/mut_results.txt, amp_basic.sh/amp_basic.txt, half_header.py, unplug.py, e2e.txt).

**The reported results hold up.** Re-run independently:
- Windows: test_board.py 228 PASS + 2 SKIP; test_kismet_v3.py 329 PASS + 1 SKIP.
- WSL: 244 and 329 PASS.
- tests/remote_e2e.sh on ports 2731/3731, against the kismet_cap_esp32c5 installed at 12:42:29 (unchanged during the run): 92 PASS, ALL OK, exit 0. In that run the held board was offered 207 ms after release and was capturing in Kismet after 3038 ms.

**Checks that found nothing wrong:**
- **Link type before "capturing" (P1):** now reported at the same point as the C helper's frame_records().
- **Watchdog:** now watches `capturing`, so a board answering in the wrong link type is also given up after 15 s.
- **`port_locked()`:** its /proc/locks test matches the C `node_locked()`: the FLOCK type, dev:inode printed `%02x:%02x:%d`, stat following links, and this process's own pid excluded.
- **Skip-and-retry for a held port:** the check runs before connect, and the retry is 5 s. The text is the C probe's text word for word.
- **--list:** leaves held boards out; exit 1 when every board is held.
- **Bluetooth LE channel (P3):** 37 is reported for a channel set and for each hop-list entry, and any channel outside 37-39 is refused. This matches the C chantranslate/chancontrol.
- **`radiotap_freq_khz`:** matches the C line for line.
- **BTLE and 802.15.4 frequency:** the signal blocks are harmless. Kismet overwrites `signal_info` from the radiotap and BTLE headers.
- **kismetdb frequency 0:** the report's explanation is right: kis_databaselogfile.cc logs `common_info.freq_khz`.
- **Exit statuses (P4):** code and text agree.

Of 29 mutations, 25 are caught by the tests. The four survivors are listed below.

**Suspected but not proven, so not listed as findings:**
1. The busy check is check-then-act. A helper whose port is closed for a moment (the ~1 s wait after a serial error or stall reopen, or the gap between a local source's helper runs) can be seen as free. A second copy of the same source would then still make Kismet close the running one. The C probe has the same window.
2. The module docstring says "Every packet carries its frequency in the signal block". A Wi-Fi record whose radiotap header has no Channel field gets no block at all, though the firmware always writes one.
3. With both a login holding '&' and --apikey given, the warning says "use an API key (--apikey ...)" even though the key is being ignored in favour of the login.
4. A BTLE hop list is reported as ["37","37",...]. This is cosmetic, and the C does the same.

findings.title: The '&' warning, --help and docstrings say a login with '&' cannot pass Kismet 'from any client'; Kismet accepts HTTP Basic auth on the websocket upgrade, which has no such limit, and the helper could use it
findings.demonstration:
Test: scratchpad fix6/review-py/amp_basic.sh, output in amp_basic.txt. It runs a Kismet on port 2731 with httpd_password=pa&ss.

Source check, kis_net_beast_httpd.cc: lines 1306-1332 read `Authorization: Basic` before anything else and check_admin_login(user, pass) straight from it. Only when that header is absent (the `else` at 1337) does it read the decoded and '&'-split query variables `user` and `password`.

Output:
```
REST with curl -u 'amp:pa&ss' (Basic): HTTP 200
query login (the helper's way, user=amp&password=pa%26ss): Handshake status 401 Unauthorized
Basic auth header, same user and password: connected, status 101
   <- KDS_OPENREQ
```
After the Basic-auth connect, Kismet took our NEWSOURCE and sent an OPENREQ.

The helper itself, with --user amp --password 'pa&ss', prints its warning ('... so this one cannot log in over the websocket; use an API key ...') and then gets 401 every 5 s.

So these user-visible claims are false, and they are headed for the wiki:
- --help (lines 1394-1396): 'cannot log in, from any client'
- the module docstring (lines 63-65)
- ampersand_in_login's docstring ('Kismet cannot take such a login from any client')
findings.suggested_fix:
In make_connector (lines 1211-1214), send the user login as a header instead of the query: `Authorization: Basic base64(user:password)`, added to WsTransport's header list next to Sec-WebSocket-Protocol. Kismet grants the same LOGON_ROLE either way. This also keeps the password out of URLs.

Then drop or narrow the '&' warning. Basic auth cannot carry a ':' in the user name, so warn about that instead if needed.

If the query login is kept, reword the warning, --help, the docstrings and the wiki text: Kismet splits the *query* login at '&'; a Basic-auth login is not affected. Also tell the C agent, whose warn_login_ampersand text makes the same claim.

findings.title: No test covers _disconnected() clearing `capturing`: reverting it leaves an unplugged board 'capturing' for ever, so the 15 s watchdog never fires, and both test files still pass
findings.demonstration:
Mutation B3 (scratchpad fix6/review-py/mut.py, applied in a scratch copy): in _disconnected, `self.synced = self.capturing = False` becomes `self.synced = False`.

Result:
```
board: 244 PASS, 0 FAIL, ALL OK
v3: 329 PASS, 0 FAIL, ALL OK
```

Consequence (scratchpad unplug.py): a board captures, then its reads raise and it cannot be reopened.
- Real code: `3 s after unplug: capturing=False synced=False`
- Mutant: `3 s after unplug: capturing=True synced=False`

Connection._watchdog now reads link.capturing, so with the mutant 'has not been capturing for 15 s' is never sent for a board that is gone. After a replug, 'capturing' is never said again either (`if not self.capturing` blocks it).
findings.suggested_fix:
Add a test_board.py check in the FakeBoard section. Let a capturing link's port fail (e.g. FakeBoard(vanish_on_mode=True) after sync, or set gone=True). Assert link.capturing is False after the error status. After it reopens and resyncs, assert a second 'capturing' status is said.

In test_kismet_v3.py, a session test with a real BoardLink whose board disappears should also see the 'has not been capturing' SHUTDOWN.

findings.title: Parity gap: BoardLink re-asks START and reopens a stalled port only while not synced, while the C helper now does so while not capturing, so a board that sends the marker and a partial header then goes quiet stays stuck until the 15 s watchdog
findings.demonstration:
Test: scratchpad fix6/review-py/half_header.py. A fake port answers START with '\n<<START>> <nonce>\n' plus the first 10 bytes of the PCAP global header, then says nothing, with the port still open.

Python BoardLink over 9 s:
```
opens at: [0.0]
commands: [(0.01, 'MODE WIFI'), (0.81, 'START ... 3aa45d99')]
statuses: [(0.0, 'FAKE opened', 'opened')]
after 9 s: synced=True capturing=False
```
That is: no second START, and no 'no answer' reopen after STALL_TIMEOUT_S. Only Connection._watchdog ends it at 15 s, followed by a full reconnect 5 s later.

The C helper now does `if (capturing(local)) continue;` (capture_esp32c5.c:1618). It then sends MODE/START again after START_RETRY_S (2 s) and calls drop_port("no answer") after STALL_TIMEOUT_S (6 s) (lines 1621-1650). Its old code used local->synced there, as the Python still does at board.py:844 (`if self.synced: continue`). The stall comment at line 867 still says 'before the stream has synced'.
findings.suggested_fix:
In BoardLink.run, use `if self.capturing: continue` in place of `if self.synced: continue`. Update the stall comment to 'before capture', as in the C.

Keep reading while synced but not capturing: _consume already handles it, since the scanner is skipped while synced. A fresh START changes the nonce, so the next marker still syncs.

Add a test_board.py case with a board that sends a half header and then goes quiet: expect a second START within about START_RETRY_S + MODE_SETTLE_S.

findings.title: The test named 'capturing, said before the first record goes on' does not check the order: moving the status after the records passes
findings.demonstration:
Mutation B8 (scratchpad mut_extra.py, applied in a scratch copy): _consume no longer says 'capturing' before the records loop. It says it only after on_packet() has run for the records, with `if self.capturing and self._last_status != '%s capturing' % self.current_port: self._status(...)`.

Result:
```

v3: 329 PASS, 0 FAIL, ALL OK
```
The check at line 619 only tests `statuses == [("FAKE capturing", "capturing")] and len(got) == 1` after the call, so it cannot see the order its name claims.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the events in one list: on_packet appends ('packet',) and on_status appends (text, kind). Assert that the list starts with ('FAKE capturing', 'capturing') and is followed by the packet. Otherwise drop 'said before the first record goes on' from the check's name.

findings.title: The radiotap test only covers one extra presence word, so `while` → `if` over the bit-31 chain survives and gives a wrong frequency (0) for headers with three presence words
findings.demonstration:
Mutation R14 (scratchpad mut.py, applied in a scratch copy): in remote.radiotap_freq_khz (remote.py:505), `while word & (1 << RADIOTAP_EXT):` becomes `if word & (1 << RADIOTAP_EXT):`.

Result:
```
v3 rc=0 fails=0
```
(329 PASS, ALL OK)

On a header with three presence words (bit 31 set in the first two), then Flags and Channel 5180 MHz:
```
base 5180000
mut-R14 0
```
The test's radiotap(ext=True) builds only a single extra word, so it cannot tell a loop from a single step. The C test harness is in the same position.
findings.suggested_fix: Let radiotap() build N extra presence words: 'ext' as a count, each word except the last with bit 31. Add a check with ext=2 (and TSFT) expecting 5745000.

fix.summary:
I checked all six review findings myself and all six were real, so all six are fixed, each with a test. Final runs all pass: Windows 233+2 SKIP and 338+1 SKIP, WSL 249 and 338, and remote_e2e.sh 93 PASS, ALL OK, exit 0.

1. **A login containing '&' can pass after all.** Kismet reads an `Authorization: Basic` header before the address, and takes the login from it as it is (kis_net_beast_httpd.cc, 1306-1332 at cfe427074). Against a real Kismet on port 2711, before the fix: the address login gives 401 for 'pa&ss' and 'a&mp', while Basic gives 200. The reverse also holds: a user name with ':' works only in the address, because Basic ends the user name at its first ':'.
   - The helper now sends a login in a Basic `Authorization` header.
   - A user name containing ':' still goes in the address, and so does an API key.
   - The only login that cannot pass is a user name with ':' plus an '&' anywhere in the login. The old '&' warning is replaced by one for that case only. The wrong 'from any client' claims are gone from the warning, --help and docstrings.
   - After the fix, the same Kismet takes '&' in either the user name or the password, a space and '%41', and a ':' user name. A ':' user name with '&' gets the warning and 401.

2. **Coverage (no bug): nothing checked that a board's `capturing` flag is cleared when it goes away.** Deleting that line passed every test (reproduced). Added:
   - a test_board.py check: the port goes away, `capturing` turns false, and 'capturing' is said again once the board is back;
   - a test_kismet_v3.py session in which a board is unplugged while capturing and the watchdog sends ERROR and SHUTDOWN.

3. **Parity gap with the C helper, reproduced.** A board that sends our marker and half a header, then goes quiet, got one START in 9 s and no reopen. `BoardLink.run` now re-asks and reopens a silent port until the board is capturing, not just until it is synced, which is what capture_esp32c5.c does. Rerun: START again at 2.0 s. Added a test_board.py case with a fake board that answers half a header.

4. **The 'said before the first record' check did not check the order.** Statuses and records now go into one list and the check asserts the order.

5. **Warning once per held spell was not tested.** New test: held, free, held again gives two warnings.

6. **The radiotap test could not tell a loop from a single step over the presence words.** `radiotap()` now builds any number of extra presence words, and the check includes three.

The six mutants the tests did not catch before are caught now: the four the reviewer found, plus a revert of each of my two fixes.

**Reviewer's unproven points:**
- The docstring said every packet carries a frequency. Narrowed: a Wi-Fi header without a Channel field gets no signal block, as in the C helper.
- The warning's API-key advice was inaccurate when --apikey was also given. It now says to use an API key 'instead of the login', which holds either way.
- The check-then-act race is still open.

**Implementer's open issues:** none could be resolved on my side.
- The kismetdb frequency of 0 for 802.15.4 and BTLE is a Kismet server limit.
- The BTLE hop list shows as ['37','37']. That is cosmetic, and the C helper does the same.
- The busy check cannot see locks held from another namespace.
- tools/fake_board.py still sends the same frames on every start. The C agent added --lacks and --silent but no variation, so my e2e workaround stays.
- The wiki is not updated.

remote_e2e.sh's login password now contains '&' and '%41', so every websocket case proves the header login against the real Kismet. There is one new check, 93 in all. Evidence is in scratchpad fix6/pyfix2: mut_before.txt, mut_after.txt, amp_before.txt, amp_after.txt, repro_before.txt, repro_after.txt, e2e-1.txt and e2e-1.capmtime.

findings.title: '&' warning, --help and docstrings wrongly said a login with '&' cannot pass Kismet 'from any client'; Basic auth on the websocket upgrade has no such limit
findings.why: Reproduced: Kismet cfe427074 reads Authorization: Basic first (kis_net_beast_httpd.cc 1306-1332). Against a real Kismet on 2711 (amp_before.txt), 'pa&ss' in the query gives 401 while Basic gives 200; a user name with ':' gives 401 with Basic and 200 in the query. Fix: make_connector sends user and password as 'Authorization: Basic base64(user:password)' through a new WsTransport authorization= argument. A user name with ':' goes in the address instead (?user=&password=), and an API key stays ?KISMET=. ampersand_in_login() is replaced by login_cannot_pass(), which is true only for a user name with ':' plus an '&' anywhere in the login. The warning, --help login paragraph and module docstring were rewritten. Tests: the address and header for an API key, for an '&' + '%41' + space + non-ASCII login, and for a ':' user name; a live FakeKismet session checks the header and a query-free request line; nine argv/env warning cases. remote_e2e.sh's password is now 'e2e&pass%41word'. amp_after.txt: '&' in user or password, space+'%41', and a ':' user name all get KDS_OPENREQ; ':'+'&' warns and gets 401. hw.summary:
The fixes work on the Pi's four real boards. I checked 12 things plus the build: 9 pass and 3 are partial, and none of the partials is caused by the fixed helper code. All four boards are reflashed, verified against the image and back in Wi-Fi.

**Build.** I synced the repo copy and ran add-to-kismet.sh, which edited capture_framework.c 3 times with no skip notes; the result is identical to WSL's patched tree. The rebuild took 174 s and I installed without sudo. It also recompiled kismet_server.cc, because the script re-copies an unchanged header with a new timestamp. The installed helper reports version 2026.09.0-cfe427074, sha256 a451120f.

**Pass:**
- **H1, websocket speed:** the C helper's first packet now arrives in 1.2-1.4 s over the websocket (it was 5.1-6.0 s before the fix). That matches --tcp (1.2-1.6 s) and the Python helper (1.4-1.8 s). Packets arrive steadily, with no 5 s bursts.
- **H2, give-up text:** the 15 s give-up text now appears in Kismet's log. For a local source, error_reason still shows 'IPC connection closed', because Kismet ignores the error frame.
- **H3, kill of the parent:** killing the C remote helper's parent ends its capture process and frees the board within 0.05 s.
- **H4, busy board:** a remote helper for a board already in use refuses every 5 s while the running capture carries on. When the first helper dies, the second takes over in 4.75-5.1 s. After close_source the port is free in 0.24 s and the helper reconnects about 5 s later.
- **H5, BTLE channel 38:** Kismet shows channel 37 with all three helpers.
- **H6, logins:** a password with a space and '%41' now logs in through the C helper. With '&' the C helper warns and gets 401. The Python helper now logs in with '&', so the task's expectation that both helpers fail holds only for C.
- **H7, stderr:** no libwebsockets notices remain. One 'queue depth 40' warning is printed per websocket connection attempt.
- **H10, old-firmware texts:** tested on the fake board. There are 0 'capturing' messages and one 'lost sync' per attempt, so they no longer alternate.

**Partial:**
- **H8, frequencies:** kismetdb still records frequency 0 for Zigbee and BTLE packets with every helper, while the device records show 2450000 and 2402000 kHz. This is a limit of Kismet's server, as the fixers said.
- **H9, four sources at once:** the C local and Python runs were clean. In the first C remote run, board 10:BD:A3:C8:7D:54 hung after switching from Wi-Fi to BLE: 0 BTLE packets in 60 s until I reset it with esptool. This is the same intermittent board hang the earlier retest saw on the same board. Two repeat runs were clean.
- **H11, reflash:** all four boards were flashed with no port held. A whole-image verify fails on every board, because the firmware writes about 2.2 KB of its settings area at boot. The parts it never writes verify exactly, and a full read-back differs only in that settings area.

**New firmware finding.** Board 38:44:BE:BF:D8:0C was in Zigbee mode when I flashed it. Afterwards it answered START in Wi-Fi but sent no packets. Under Kismet it showed 'capturing (wifi)' with 0 packets and no error, and an esptool reset did not clear it. I reproduced this by flashing it again from Zigbee mode. Switching it to BLE and back to Wi-Fi cures it, and flashing from Wi-Fi mode works. That board was flashed three times and ends working.

**Other open points:** the two helpers still differ when a BTLE channel set is refused. The C helper keeps capturing on 37; the Python helper errors, reconnects and loses the channel lock. Kismet sometimes starts two re-opens of a source at once (a known Kismet race). Details and evidence paths are in the problems list.

**End state.** Nothing I started is running, the ports are free and /tmp/hw3 is kept. The evidence (423 files plus SHA256SUMS) is in scratchpad\hw3. The repo is unchanged and nothing was committed.
